title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
This is a synthetic alteration of a real photograph of identifiable people, published as if it were authentic. The image was changed at the point of production, before it reached the banner, and the change was not disclosed to the people in it or to the audience. The failure sits in the gap between an institution's stated rule and the workflow that produced the material: Stanford's policy barred using AI to alter images of Stanford people, and the alteration and the silence around it both ran against that policy.

Catching it required nothing exotic. A comparison of the banner against the original photograph, by a person, before publication would have surfaced the substitution and the reshaping of the other students. A disclosure line would have surfaced the AI use even without a comparison. The review Stanford now says it will build into Residential and Dining Enterprises materials is the check that was absent when the banner went out.

What is not established is who performed the alteration, whether it was deliberate, and what consequences follow beyond the training and review Stanford has said it will provide. The reports describe a policy violation confirmed by the university, not a finding of intent.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
The original photo showed Billy Ramirez with two other students at a Lunar New Year party in 2024. Stanford’s dining service posted it online. When Stanford used the image on banners last week, Ramirez was replaced by an image of a Black woman, and the other students were made to look thinner. Ramirez, a Hispanic senior majoring in human biology, said he found it upsetting and learned about it from a friend.

Stanford said Tuesday it used AI to alter the original image. It said its policy does not allow using AI to produce or alter images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements. The alteration and lack of disclosure violated that policy. Stanford is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to provide more training and ensure proper review of all materials.
title_en: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad
